quiz.question: What does the `new` keyword do when used with a class?

answers.answer: It defines a new class blueprint
It creates an independent instance of the class
It copies all methods from another class
It deletes the previous instance of the class

quiz.explanation: The `new` keyword creates a new instance (object) from the class blueprint. Each instance is an independent copy with its own property values.

quiz.question: If two objects are created from the same class, what is true about them?

answers.answer: They share the same property values and changing one changes the other
They must have different property names
They start with the same shape but are independent copies
Only the first object gets the class properties

quiz.explanation: Every object created from the same class starts with the same shape (same properties and methods), but each one is an independent copy that can be modified without affecting others.
